frames.narration: A chat request arrives with an 8,000 token prompt. The GPU holds 16 GB of weights; the setup (80 GB, 10% reserved) leaves 56 GB for KV cache.
Prefill: all 8,192 prompt tokens go through the model in one parallel pass. Lots of arithmetic per byte moved, so this phase is compute-bound: about 0.65 s here.
Every layer produces a key and a value vector per token, and they are stored. 8,192 tokens x 128 KiB per token is about 1.07 GB for this one conversation.
The first token goes back to the user. Time to first token is about 0.65 s, almost entirely prefill. This is the number that grows with prompt length.

Decode: each next token is one pass for one new token. The GPU reads all 16 GB of weights plus this 1.07 GB cache from memory: 17.1 GB at 2 TB/s is about 8.5 ms. Memory-bandwidth-bound, with the arithmetic units mostly idle.
Tokens stream out one per step: inter-token latency about 8.5 ms, roughly 117 tokens/s for this single user. The GPU is busy but badly used.

More users arrive and share each step. With 52 sequences a step reads 16 GB + 52 x 1.07 GB = 71.8 GB, about 36 ms. Each user now gets about 28 tokens/s, but the GPU produces 1,447 tokens/s in total, 12 times more.

The 53rd request does not fit: there is no room for another 1.07 GB. It waits in the queue (or is rejected), while the GPU still has arithmetic to spare. With 32 kv heads instead of 8 the cache is 4 times larger and only 13 users fit.
